title: Silent Arbitration: How Large Language Models Resolve Co-Authoritative Conflicting Instructions
abstract: arXiv:2611.27444v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models increasingly receive high-level instructions about roles, values, interests, and communication style. Such instructions can conflict even when a prompt assigns them equal authority and provides no priority rule. We study co-authoritative persona conflict, in which a single prompt jointly assigns two opposing personas. Across eight conflict types grounded in published source material and five LLMs, we measure conflict acknowledgment, resolution strategy, and directional stance. Models acknowledge incompatibility in 72% of direct checks but explicitly surface it in only 22% of task responses, revealing silent arbitration. Dominance accounts for 45% of dual-persona responses, and 35% of compromise-labeled responses retain directional lean. translated_title: 静默仲裁：大型语言模型如何解决同等权威的冲突指令
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地接收关于角色、价值观、利益和沟通风格的高级指令。即使提示词赋予这些指令同等权威且未提供优先级规则，它们之间也可能发生冲突。我们研究了同权威人格冲突，即单个提示词同时分配两个对立的人格。基于已发表源材料中的八种冲突类型，我们在五个大语言模型上测量了冲突承认度、解决策略和方向性立场。模型在72%的直接检查中承认不兼容性，但在任务响应中仅有22%明确表达出来，这揭示了“静默仲裁”现象。支配性策略占双重人格响应的45%，而35%被标记为妥协的响应仍保留了方向性倾向。提示词框架对仲裁可见形式的改变远大于普通的改述变化。这些发现表明，评估指令遵循应当……
tldr: 研究发现大语言模型在面对同等权威的冲突人格指令时会进行“静默仲裁”——虽然在直接检查中72%会承认冲突，但在实际任务响应中仅有22%明确告知用户，其余情况下模型默默采用某一方的立场而不透明地解决冲突。
en_tdlr: LLMs silently arbitrate between co-authoritative conflicting personas—acknowledging the conflict in 72% of direct checks but explicitly surfacing it in only 22% of task responses, often adopting a directional stance without transparently informing users.
